Subject: Cause analysis and timeline — ClearPay EU pool (2027-11-10)

Hi Samir / Aisha,

Attached are the detailed artifacts: an aggregated request timeline (inference-timeline-20271110.csv) and the error bundle (clearpay-error-log-20271110.tar.gz). Below is a distilled technical narrative plus our recommended immediate actions. I kept the timeline precise and action-oriented.

Executive summary (non-technical):
- Root cause: transient memory pressure on the NVMe cache tier on the EU dedicated nodes, triggered by a short-lived cache retention mis-evaluation combined with a rare kernel fallback path that increased memory allocations for KV lookups. This caused bursty GC/IO stalls and a small number of request timeouts.
- Impact: 04:37–05:05 UTC — median token latency increased from ~120ms to ~420ms; ~0.7% of requests returned 5xx during the window. No data loss.
- Immediate mitigations taken: pinned the affected nodes to the stable kernel, refreshed KV cache hot paths, and temporarily routed traffic across an additional reserved pool to reduce load on the EU nodes.

Detailed timeline (UTC):
- 04:30 — normal traffic; periodic background cache compaction job started (configured to run every 4 hours).
- 04:37 — minor spike in cache eviction due to a mis-estimated retention threshold (metrics show surge in eviction rate).
- 04:39 — kernel fallback engaged for a small subset of requests; observed increase in memory allocations per request (traced to a particular attention kernel build).
- 04:45 — IO queue length on NVMe increases; GC cycles become longer, token generation latency rises.
- 04:50 — retries from client side amplify load; autoscaler did not trigger additional capacity quickly because burst window was below autoscaler sensitivity window.
- 05:05 — routing adjustment and node pinning completed; latency returned to baseline by 05:12.

Root cause analysis summary:
1) A configuration edge case in the cache retention estimator allowed higher-than-expected eviction during the compaction window.
2) The eviction pattern interacted with a less-common kernel code-path (a fallback attention kernel used for long-shard inputs) that allocates additional transient buffers.
3) The autoscaling sensitivity threshold and retry amplification by the client created a transient overloaded condition before the autoscaler reacted.

Action register (owners & ETA):
- Short-term (<=72h):
  • Disable compaction overlap with peak windows for EU dedicated pools (owner: Jonas Weber) — ETA: 2027-11-13
  • Back out kernel fallback to stable build on EU nodes (owner: Ops Infra team, contact: Soojin Lee) — ETA: 2027-11-12 (completed)
  • Implement temporary routing guard (SRE) to limit retry amplification impact (owner: Ben Carter) — ETA: 2027-11-12
- Medium-term (2–4 weeks):
  • Tweak cache retention estimator to include workload variance safety margin (owner: Research/Applied ML, Jonas) — ETA: 2027-12-01
  • Reduce autoscaler sensitivity window and add burst-detection heuristics (owner: Platform Autoscale team) — ETA: 2027-12-05
- Long-term (quarter):
  • Harden fallback kernel path to avoid large transient buffers (owner: Runtime Engineering) — ETA: 2028-02-15

Attachments included: inference-timeline-20271110.csv, clearpay-error-log-20271110.tar.gz, mitigation-checklist-v1.docx

We are classifying this as a reliability incident with code-level and configuration contributors. We will prepare a short non-technical customer-facing summary for Procurement/Compliance (Sofia), and an internal post-incident review doc for engineering (Marissa).

If you need a deeper dive or a short video walkthrough of the traces, I can schedule a 30-minute session.

Best,
Jonas
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

- What we did: We quickly reverted the affected runtime change on your EU nodes, adjusted routing to reduce load during the event, and collected logs and traces for a detailed review.
- Impact: The event increased median token latency for affected requests; approximately 0.7% of requests returned an error during the window. There was no data exposure.

  • Planned checks: we will run a verification run against your traffic pattern on 2027-11-18 and share the results.
  • Follow-up: We'll deliver a timeline of the engineering fixes and a plan to prevent recurrence (ETA: 2027-12-05 for configuration/autoscaler changes).
